newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Energy to split in two - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Energy to split in two - WSJ.

text.p: Santa Fe Energy Resources Inc will announce Wednesday plans to split into two separate publicly traded companies, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.

The company will take public its California operations - about 15 percent of the company - later this year, and call it Monterey Resources. The initial public offering is intended to raise about $115 million, the article said.
In the second quarter of next year, the company plans to spin off the rest of Monterey to Santa Fe shareholders, depending on whether the transaction can be ruled tax-free, the Journal said.

Chase Securities Inc, a unit of Chase Manhattan Corp and Petrie Parkman & Co of Denver are Santa Fe Energy's advisers in the move, while Goldman Sachs is expected to be the lead underwriter in the offering, the article said.
